encounters.cc: Aching wrists and ankles for 10 days with mild morning stiffness and new painless oral sore

lines: Aching wrists and ankles for 10 days with mild morning stiffness and new painless oral sore
The patient returns for follow-up of systemic lupus erythematosus diagnosed three months prior.
She describes mild morning stiffness and difficulty opening jars.
She notes that she recently developed a painless sore inside her cheek.
- History of acute promyelocytic leukemia (in remission)
- Laparoscopic appendectomy during second trimester of pregnancy
She has no family history of similar symptoms, but her mother has hypothyroidism.
Alcohol: Occasional social use (≤1 drink per week).
On physical examination, there is mild swelling of several metacarpophalangeal and proximal interphalangeal joints, as well as a shallow ulcer on the buccal mucosa.
Laboratory studies reveal a hemoglobin of 11.2 g/dL, hematocrit of 33.6%, white blood cell count of 4,200/µL, and platelet count of 55,000/µL.

encounters.cc: 8 hours of progressive abdominal pain migrating from umbilicus to right lower quadrant with emesis

lines: 8 hours of progressive abdominal pain migrating from umbilicus to right lower quadrant with emesis

The patient is a 28-year-old female with systemic lupus erythematosus under active rheumatology management since January 2020, Crohn's disease, and maintenance immunosuppressive therapy who presents with acute abdominal pain.
The pain began as vague discomfort around the umbilicus and has now localized to the right lower quadrant.
She has experienced two episodes of non-bloody, non-bilious emesis and reports subjective fever and chills.
She has had no vaginal bleeding, leakage of fluid, or dysuria.
She has had regular prenatal care with no complications until now.
- History of acute promyelocytic leukemia (in remission)
- Laparoscopic appendectomy during second trimester of pregnancy
Alcohol: Occasional social use (≤1 drink per week).
Her temperature is 38.4°C (101.1°F), pulse is 114/min, and blood pressure is 98/64 mm Hg.
Abdominal examination reveals focal tenderness in the right lower quadrant with voluntary guarding.
A speculum exam shows a closed cervix with no discharge.
The fetal heart rate is 170/min with moderate variability, no decelerations, and intermittent contractions are noted on external tocometry.
Her white blood cell count is 17,900/mm³, and urinalysis is normal.

encounters.cc: 6-month history of intermittent abdominal pain, bloody diarrhea, and unintentional weight loss

lines: 6-month history of intermittent abdominal pain, bloody diarrhea, and unintentional weight loss

The patient is a 29-year-old female with a history of systemic lupus erythematosus diagnosed in January 2020 and acute appendicitis treated in July 2020 who presents to the clinic with a 6-month history of intermittent abdominal pain, diarrhea, and unintentional weight loss.
She reports that her bowel movements are sometimes bloody and often accompanied by a feeling of incomplete evacuation.
- History of acute promyelocytic leukemia (in remission)
- Laparoscopic appendectomy during second trimester of pregnancy
She denies any family history of gastrointestinal diseases.
Alcohol: Occasional social use (≤1 drink per week).
On examination, she appears underweight and has mild tenderness in the right lower quadrant.
Perianal inspection reveals skin tags and a small fissure.
Biopsy of the affected areas shows transmural inflammation and non-caseating granulomas.
Colonoscopy demonstrates segmental areas of inflamed mucosa with linear ulcers and cobblestoning.

encounters.cc: Persistent oozing from venipuncture sites and spontaneous bruising

lines: Persistent oozing from venipuncture sites and spontaneous bruising
The patient is a 29-year-old female with systemic lupus erythematosus, Crohn's disease, and prior acute promyelocytic leukemia in remission who presents with bleeding symptoms.
She reports that over the past day, nurses have needed to change her dressings more frequently due to steady blood seepage.
She has also noticed bruising developing on her arms and legs without any associated trauma.
She denies recent nosebleeds, heavy menstrual bleeding, or gastrointestinal symptoms.
- History of acute promyelocytic leukemia (in remission)
Cytogenetic studies confirmed a t(15;17) translocation, and her oncologist had expressed concern about her risk for coagulopathy related to treatment.
- Laparoscopic appendectomy during second trimester of pregnancy
Alcohol: Occasional social use (≤1 drink per week).
Her blood pressure is normal, and she is afebrile.
She is alert and oriented but appears pale and mildly tachycardic.
Physical examination reveals scattered petechiae on her lower extremities and non-tender ecchymoses overlying her forearms.
There is no hepatosplenomegaly, lymphadenopathy, or focal neurologic deficit.
Her central line site and several IV lines have persistent oozing despite local pressure.
Initial labs reveal anemia and thrombocytopenia.
Laboratory studies and a blood smear are shown:

encounters.cc: Intermittent fevers, chills, drenching sweats, and myalgias after returning from sub-Saharan Africa

lines: Intermittent fevers, chills, drenching sweats, and myalgias after returning from sub-Saharan Africa

The patient is a 30-year-old female with systemic lupus erythematosus, Crohn's disease, and acute promyelocytic leukemia in remission on hydroxychloroquine, prednisone, and azathioprine, who returns from a 3-week volunteer trip to a rural farming region in sub-Saharan Africa.

She reports that while abroad she took a daily tablet prescribed for prevention of a parasitic illness, but over the last 5 days she has developed intermittent fevers, chills, drenching sweats, malaise, and diffuse myalgias.
- Acute Promyelocytic Leukemia with Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (diagnosed 2021-07-15)
- History of acute promyelocytic leukemia (in remission)
- Laparoscopic appendectomy during second trimester of pregnancy
Alcohol: Occasional social use (≤1 drink per week).
She denies respiratory or urinary symptoms.
Temperature is 39.5 °C (103.1 °F), pulse is 110/min, blood pressure is 104/68 mmHg, and respirations are 20/min.
On examination, she appears fatigued and diaphoretic.
The sclerae are anicteric, lungs are clear, and the abdomen is soft but mildly enlarged in the left upper quadrant.
Laboratory testing reveals normocytic anemia and thrombocytopenia.
A peripheral blood smear demonstrates intracellular ring-shaped inclusions within red blood cells.

encounters.cc: Routine prenatal visit with concern for decreased fetal movements

lines: Routine prenatal visit with concern for decreased fetal movements
She returns for prenatal care with systemic lupus erythematosus, Crohn disease, and leukemia.
She reports no rash, joint pain, or other lupus-related symptoms during pregnancy.
However, she is concerned because she feels the baby's movements have decreased over the past week.
- Acute Promyelocytic Leukemia with Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (diagnosed 2021-07-15)
- History of acute promyelocytic leukemia (in remission)
She has a history of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE).
Her obstetric history is significant for one previous miscarriage at 10 weeks gestation.
- Laparoscopic appendectomy during second trimester of pregnancy
She has been stable on hydroxychloroquine and low-dose prednisone.
Alcohol: Occasional social use (≤1 drink per week).
On examination, her blood pressure is 120/78 mmHg, heart rate is 88 bpm, and temperature is 98.6°F (37°C)
Fetal heart rate monitoring shows a persistent fetal heart rate of 90 bpm.
There are no signs of fetal distress or uterine contractions.
- Complete blood count: Within normal limits
- Urinalysis: No proteinuria or active sediment

encounters.cc: 24-hour history of right-sided abdominal pain migrating from umbilicus to right upper quadrant with nausea

lines: 24-hour history of right-sided abdominal pain migrating from umbilicus to right upper quadrant with nausea

This 31-year-old female with systemic lupus erythematosus, Crohn's disease, and a history of acute appendicitis in 2020 presents to the emergency department with a 24-hour history of right-sided abdominal pain.
She describes the pain as sharp and constant, initially located around the umbilicus but now localized to the right mid-to-upper quadrant.
She also reports nausea but no vomiting, fever, or changes in bowel habits.
- Acute Promyelocytic Leukemia with Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (diagnosed 2021-07-15)
- History of acute promyelocytic leukemia (in remission)
She has had an uncomplicated pregnancy thus far.
- Laparoscopic appendectomy during second trimester of pregnancy
Alcohol: Occasional social use (≤1 drink per week).
On examination, her temperature is 37.8°C (100°F), heart rate is 98 bpm, and blood pressure is 125/75 mmHg.
Abdominal examination reveals tenderness and guarding in the right mid-to-upper quadrant with a negative Murphy's sign.
Laboratory tests show a white blood cell count of 12,000/µL with a left shift.
An obstetric ultrasound confirms a viable intrauterine pregnancy and no evidence of cholecystitis or pyelonephritis.
